summary: Added a READ-ONLY auto-pickup dry-run preview. core.auto_pickup_dryrun(runner, topic) reports the task auto_pickup WOULD claim WITHOUT mutating the parent queue and WITHOUT touching the write gate. It never invokes the write-gated `auto-pickup` command; it reuses only the read-only `export` command (pending_for_runner) and replicates the exact candidate-selection predicate of taskctl.cmd_auto_pickup (unclaimed + pending + runner-matched + topic-matched, first). Exposed as MCP tool geoai_task_auto_pickup_dryrun. Additive only: real claim semantics in core.py/server.py are unchanged and auto_pickup stays behind GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES.

public_api.core.auto_pickup_dryrun(runner, topic=No: read-only preview dict {ok, dry_run, would_claim_task_id, candidate, filtering{runner_filter,topic_filter,pending_for_runner_topic,eligible_unclaimed,excluded_already_claimed}, mutation{queue_mutated,write_gate_bypassed,write_command_invoked,real_auto_pickup_write_gated,writes_allowed_env}, source_command, export_returncode}
public_api.core.eligible_dryrun_candidates(rows, ru: pure -> ordered eligible cards mirroring cmd_auto_pickup (unclaimed+pending+runner+topic)

neural_bridge_note: The dry-run selection is a DETERMINISTIC MIRROR of taskctl.cmd_auto_pickup's own candidate predicate (a preview/validator over the queue substrate, Layer 1), NOT a runtime cue router owning cognition. It decides no capability the model must learn; it only reports what the existing deterministic queue command would do. A future LEARNED task-routing/abstain policy (which runner/topic a worker session should pursue) remains tracked separately and is out of scope for this read-only preview.
no_launch_no_switch_marker: This change adds NO process-launch code and NO workflow switch: no subprocess beyond the pre-existing read-only `export` call, no runtime switch to MCP, no write-gate disable. The only subprocess in the dry-run path is `taskctl export` (not a WRITE_COMMAND).
